nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices and every pair $(u, v)$ in $L$, the cover that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ contains $u$ or $v$.
nodes.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER covers every listed pair

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that for every edge $uv$ of $G$, $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ is in $L$. Then the cover that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ is a vertex cover of $G$.
nodes.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns a vertex cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$, and let $C$ be the cover that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$. Then there is a sublist $A$ of $L$ such that pairs at different positions of $A$ are vertex-disjoint, every pair in $L$ shares an endpoint with some pair in $A$, a vertex lies in $C$ exactly when it is an endpoint…
nodes.title: The edges APPROX-VERTEX-COVER takes form a maximal matching of the listed pairs

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices, the cost of APPROX-VERTEX-COVER on $L$ is the length of $L$: one unit per listed pair.
nodes.title: Running time of APPROX-VERTEX-COVER

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices that lists exactly the edges of $G$, each in at least one orientation: $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$, and for every edge $uv$ of $G$, $(u, v)$ or $(v, u)$ is in $L$. Then the cover $C$ that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ is a vertex cover of $G$ and $|C| \le 2\tau(G)$, where $\tau(G) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$…
nodes.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER is a 2-approximation

nodes.summary: Given a list $L$ of ordered pairs of vertices, APPROX-VERTEX-COVER starts from the empty cover and goes through $L$ in order: a pair $(u, v)$ with $u$ or $v$ already in the cover is skipped, and otherwise both $u$ and $v$ are added to the cover. It returns the final cover, a finite set of vertices, at a cost of one unit per pair of $L$.
nodes.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$. Then for every vertex cover $S$ of $G$, finite or infinite, the cover $C$ that APPROX-VERTEX-COVER returns on $L$ satisfies $|C| \le 2|S|$, with sizes in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$.
nodes.title: APPROX-VERTEX-COVER is at most twice any vertex cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $S$ a vertex cover of $G$, $C_0$ a finite set of vertices with $|C_0| \le 2|C_0 \cap S|$, and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$. Then the cover $C$ that the vertex cover scan returns on $L$ starting from $C_0$ satisfies $|C| \le 2|C \cap S|$.
nodes.title: Counting invariant of the vertex cover scan

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph, $C_0$ a finite set of vertices, and $L$ a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$ for every $(u, v)$ in $L$, and let $C$ be the cover that the vertex cover scan returns on $L$ starting from $C_0$. Then there is a sublist $A$ of $L$ such that neither endpoint of any pair in $A$ lies in $C_0$, pairs at different positions of $A$ are vertex-disjoint, a…
nodes.title: Matching invariant of the vertex cover scan

nodes.summary: For every finite set $C$ of vertices and every list of pairs of vertices, the cover returned by the vertex cover scan starting from $C$ on that list contains $C$.
nodes.title: The vertex cover scan only adds vertices

nodes.summary: For every finite set $C$ of vertices and every list $L$ of pairs of vertices, the running time of the vertex cover scan starting from $C$ on $L$ is the length of $L$.
nodes.title: Running time of the vertex cover scan

nodes.summary: Given a finite set $C$ of vertices and a list of pairs of vertices, the scan processes the pairs in order, starting from the cover $C$ and charging one time unit per pair. A pair $(u, v)$ is covered when $u$ or $v$ is already in the current cover; a covered pair is skipped, and an uncovered pair adds both $u$ and $v$ to the cover. The scan returns the cover reached after the last pair.
nodes.title: Vertex cover scan

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
